result.document_summary: An SF.gov Rent Board news item announcing that Section 37.10C of the San Francisco Rent Ordinance, prohibiting algorithmic devices used to set rents, took effect October 14, 2024.
result.notes: Single instrument (S.F. Rent Ordinance Section 37.10C). The page does not state coverage limits or exemptions, so coverage is left empty. The page says the law applies to residential units in San Francisco and does not name any other law it interacts with.

rules.title: Ban on algorithmic devices used to set rents (Rent Ordinance Section 37.10C)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to sell or use algorithmic devices, such as software that analyzes nonpublic competitor rental data to recommend what rent to charge for a vacant unit, to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units. A tenant or the City Attorney may bring a civil action over a violation.
rules.key_value: Ban on sale or use of algorithmic rent-setting devices
rules.quoted_span: The law prohibits the sale or use of such algorithmic devices and allows a tenant or the City Attorney to bring a civil action if they believe an entity is in violation of the law.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to the sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco.
